allowed_dependency_manifest.content: For each fixed integer n greater than 1, consider the function E_n(x) = floor(n x) minus the sum over integers k with 1 <= k <= n of floor(k x) divided by k. forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

payload.role_in_assembly: Identify the unique endpoint numerator that can saturate the bound.

domain_restrictions: k is an integer summation index with 1 less than or equal to k and k less than or equal to n
floor is the greatest integer less than or equal to its real input
root_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For each fixed integer n greater than 1, consider the function E_n(x) = floor(n x) minus the sum over integers k with 1 <= k <= n of floor(k x) divided by k. The task is to determine the set of real x values for which E_n(x) attains its maximum over all real x, and to determine the corresponding maximal value M(n).
quantifier_order: for all integers n with n greater than 1
there exists a real number x_star

variables.name: n
variables.role: fixed parameter with constraint n greater than 1

variables.name: k
variables.role: summation index, restricted to k from 1 through n

variables.name: x
variables.role: variable over which the expression is maximized

variables.name: y
variables.role: arbitrary competitor value to define maximality

variables.name: E_n(x)
variables.role: defined expression: floor(n x) minus sum from k = 1 to n of floor(k x) divided by k

variables.name: M(n)
variables.role: the maximal value of E_n(x) over all real x, depends on n

variables.name: x_star
variables.role: a real number where the maximum is achieved; may depend on n

witness_dependencies: x_star depends on n (the maximizing real numbers may vary with the given integer n)

domain_restrictions: n is an integer and n > 1
a is an integer and 1 <= a <= n - 1
k is an integer with 1 <= k <= n - 1
r_k is the least nonnegative residue modulo n, hence 0 <= r_k <= n - 1
The inequality r_1 >= r_2 >= ... >= r_{n-1} is asserted over the finite index set k = 1, ..., n - 1
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every integer n > 1 and every integer a with 1 <= a <= n - 1, define for each integer k with 1 <= k <= n - 1 the value r_k to be the least nonnegative residue modulo n of Res_n(a,k). If the sequence satisfies r_1 >= r_2 >= ... >= r_{n-1}, then a equals n - 1.
quantifier_order: for all integers n with n > 1
for all integers a with 1 <= a <= n - 1
for all integers k with 1 <= k <= n - 1 (in the definition of r_k)
if the inequality condition holds for the resulting sequence r_1, ..., r_{n-1}

variables.name: a
variables.role: base parameter, with restriction 1 <= a <= n - 1

variables.name: k
variables.role: index for a finite sequence, with restriction 1 <= k <= n - 1

variables.name: r_k
variables.role: least nonnegative residue of Res_n(a,k), so it satisfies 0 <= r_k <= n - 1

variables.name: Res_n(a,k)
variables.role: an integer-valued expression defined in terms of n, a, and k whose residue modulo n is taken to define r_k

witness_dependencies: r_k depends on (n, a, k) through the value Res_n(a,k) and then taking its least nonnegative residue modulo n
The inequality condition depends on the entire sequence {r_k} for k from 1 to n - 1

payload.statement_nl: For every integer n>1 and every integer a with 1 <= a <= n-1, let r_k be the least nonnegative residue Res_n(a,k) for k=1,...,n-1. If r_1 >= r_2 >= ... >= r_{n-1}, then a = n-1.
